items.q: The ~94 inch measurement you gave — width or depth?
What did the long-wall tape measure read? (The photo shows the span, not the number.)
The tile medallion above the range — keep it, or let it go?
items.why: It's the diamond-patterned tile panel set into the backsplash directly above your cooktop — a framed square of small diamonds with an ornate border, surrounded by the plain travertine. It's in the house today. You generated the new kitchen style both with it and without it, so we're asking rather than guessing. Default if you say nothing: keep it — it was deleted once by inference and restored by your own correction.

items.q: From the run wall to the near face of the dining ceiling beam — how far?
items.why: 📏 ONE TRIP, TWO TAPES — do this one together with the cabinet-next-to-the-stove tape. Your three photographs proved there is ONE beam, not three, and two were deleted on that evidence. But a photograph settles how many things there are, not where they are — in your photo the real beam sits nearer the camera than anything modelled, and nobody nudged it to match by eye. This is the oldest unresolved item in the walls lane and it has now blocked three times.

items.q: The cabinet next to the stove — how wide is its front, from the stove to its far edge?
items.why: 📏 ONE TRIP, TWO TAPES — pair this with the ceiling beam one above; you are standing in the same house and the second costs about thirty seconds. ONE tape, FIVE answers: this single number settles how long the angled stove wall really is, where both ends of the counter run sit, where the counter seam falls, and the anchor everything east of the kitchen is measured from. We have it at 14.2 inches each side; one reading of the scan suggests about 31. Those are different rooms. It is not a leftover ask — five separate calculations converge here and none of them can answer it alone. It also decides whether the stove wall is right, and the stove, hood and tile panel are all sized to it — the first thing anyone looks at.

items.q: At 12 seconds your dad says something like 'pushed to that table' — did he mean 'tape line'?
items.why: The transcription is ambiguous there and it was recorded as ambiguous rather than resolved. There IS blue floor tape marking the cut, so 'tape line' fits — but one word from you settles it instead of us picking.

items.why: We can read the tape but not what it spans: the hook sits on bare tile, the far end is out of frame, and the blade never crosses the blue cut-line, so the number can't be attributed to anything. Just the two endpoints, and the reading if you have it.
